messages.content: Create at most two reusable medical-image reading skills from this training example. The saved answer/reason may be wrong. Return only JSON {"skills":[{"category":"general or one supplied official category","trigger":"when to apply","steps":["concrete image check","how to distinguish alternatives"]}]}. No case/patient ID, option letter, figure number, patient-specific number, copied question, or rule merely repeating the reference diagnosis. General medical findings are allowed. Based solely on the chest X-ray findings in Figure 1, which of the following best characterizes the opacities observed in the right lung base, considering the patient's history and current clinical context?

A. Consolidations with air bronchograms, consistent with bacterial pneumonia
B. Patchy ground-glass opacities with peripheral distribution, suggestive of COVID-19 infection
C. Homogeneous opacities with well-defined margins, indicative of lung metastases
D. Diffuse nodular opacities with central distribution, characteristic of sarcoidosis
E. Linear opacities with reticular pattern, indicative of interstitial lung disease
F. Focal dense opacity with calcification, suggestive of a pulmonary infarct
